title: PP comm optimization: replace send with partial send + allgather (#6695)
gain_evidence: Communication optimization for pipeline parallelism, we observed 5% improvement in throughput for llama 3.1 405b.

experiments.name: pp_send_partial_allgather
experiments.workload: Author ran Llama 3.1 405B under pipeline parallelism and observed ~5% throughput improvement from replacing the full inter-stage tensor send with a sliced (partial) send followed by a TP all-gather (reported via a before/after plot in a comment, no tabulated numbers).
experiments.note: Diff adds an all_gather_group arg to GroupCoordinator.send_tensor_dict / recv_tensor_dict in parallel_state.py: when set, each PP send transmits only a 1/world_size slice (tensor.reshape(all_gather_size,-1)[rank]) and the receiver reconstructs the full tensor via all_gather over the TP group. worker_base.py passes get_tp_group() as all_gather_group. Number source: PR body '5% improvement in throughput for llama 3.1 405b' plus a before/after screenshot in a comment; no absolute tok/s values.

reported.scope: end-to-end serving throughput for Llama 3.1 405B across pipeline + tensor parallel ranks; the win is reduced inter-stage PP communication volume on a multi-GPU/multi-node interconnect
reported.scale_short: Author's ~5% is whole-run serving throughput for a 405B model over PP+TP on real interconnect, shown only as a plot with no absolute numbers; it is a distributed-comm effect, not CPU-reproducible. TO MAKE 1:1: on a multi-GPU box with PP>1 and TP>1, benchmark serving tok/s with and without all_gather_group on send/recv_tensor_dict, isolating the partial-send + all-gather path.
reported.scale_note: The optimization shrinks each PP send to a 1/TP slice and rebuilds the tensor with a TP all-gather, trading send bandwidth for an all-gather; the benefit depends on PP/TP sizes and interconnect, and the author noted they tested few scenarios and saw no regressions. No absolute throughput published (plot only), and the path only exercises across real parallel ranks, so magnitude is not reproducible on our single-host CPU bench.
